extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a state bar has suspended a practitioner. Covers notice, opportunity to respond, default consequences, publication, and administrative steps (Customer Numbers/PKI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline may request that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a State authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requests imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the state bar (here, Oregon). Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty (40) days to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely response may raise the §11.24(d)(1) grounds to contest reciprocal imposition. The Notice was mailed by certified mail and delivered; the 40-day response period is the procedural window to create a genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default consequence — no genuine issue of material fact if no response
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to the Notice and Order supports imposition of identical discipline without contest; non-response functions as a default factual posture for the USPTO proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical suspension (duration and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for 120 days, effective on the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline imposed by USPTO is identical in duration to the state-imposed suspension (here, 120 days). The Final Order expressly orders the same scope (patent, trademark and other non-patent matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Official Gazette — required Notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette containing the practitioner's name, registration number, the fact of suspension, the predicate state suspension, the regulation violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) here), relevant dates, and citation to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes a template 'NOTICE OF SUSPENSION' text specifying required information (name, registration number, state suspension summary, statutory/regulatory citations) and a reference to disciplinary decisions being posted in the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures reciprocal disciplinary information is shared with relevant state authorities and courts; §11.59 governs notice dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §11.58 sets out post-disciplinary duties (e.g., client notification, file transfer/retention, withdrawal obligations); the Final Order requires adherence to those duties as part of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The US PTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative measures to remove practitioner access to USPTO electronic filing and systems while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or being added to USPTO Customer Numbers until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, and shall not have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block on regaining electronic access or associational access during the suspension period until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for state suspension cited — failure to respond to disciplinary inquiries (Oregon RPC 8.1(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Reali failed to respond to inquiries from the Oregon disciplinary authority, in violation of Oregon Rule of Professional Conduct 8.1(a)(2), which led to his suspension from the practice of law in Oregon for 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State disciplinary findings (such as failure to respond to disciplinary inquiries) can serve as the predicate misconduct for reciprocal USPTO discipline under §11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by certified mail and proof of delivery as procedural predicate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. 70143490000038972241) and was delivered to Respondent on June 22, 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service (e.g., certified mail with delivery) of the Notice and Order is documented and supports proceeding; demonstrates compliance with notice requirements before imposing reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation for action — 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes/regulations provide the legal authority for imposing reciprocal discipline, publishing notices, and related administrative actions.
